history.summary: NOT A CONVENTIONAL HINDU TEMPLE - it is a Satra, a Vaishnavite monastery of the Ekasarana (Neo-Vaishnavite) tradition of Assam; documented here as a religious site. Founded in 1570 by Mahapurush Madhavdev, the chief disciple of Srimanta Sankardev, who spent 14 years and six months here; the house where he lived and composed his works is preserved nearby. Ahom king Pramatta Singha later built the doul on the premises. The walls carry paintings of the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, and the main Namghar (Kirtonghar) houses the Bhagawat Thapona. The satra sits in Sundaridiya village, about 14 km from Barpeta town. Coordinates are of Sundaridia village (verify - exact satra position unconfirmed).

town_description: Barpeta is the district headquarters town of Barpeta district in lower Assam, about 120 km northwest of Guwahati. It is a historic centre of the Ekasarana (Neo-Vaishnavite) tradition, home to the famous Barpeta Satra, and known for its Doul Utsav celebrations and traditional crafts.
